# Appendix: Ask Us Anything

Questions are edited for clarity. Some questions are also answered on the wrapup page.

## Theme & Story

**Q: It was really cool that the story was a central part of this hunt, and it felt like the metas were also built around it. At what point was this decision made?**

A: This was the core goal of the theme proposal, so it was our main goal from the moment the theme was decided.

**Q: This year's hunt seemed more "vanilla" than the past three iterations. What was the overall design philosophy?**

A: This year the winning theme proposal put most of its “weirdness points” into the story. We thought that writing an honest story with fun puzzles would make for a fun puzzle hunt.

**Q: Were the characters' stories inspired by real-life experiences?**

A: Indirectly? There’s certainly bits of our and our friends’ experiences reflected, in that we write what we know? But the central storylines are primarily derived from the metas, plus whatever fun ideas came up during brainstorming (none of us owns a café but it made for a nice setting).

**Q: How many of you are embroiled in 1/3rd life crises right now because that part really felt like it came from the heart? (Genuine question, speaking as someone a few days older than Lam who's going through Changes along with all my friends.)**

A:

* I am unemployed
* I just got fired
* I have questioned my gender

**Q: Can we have a cute café cat next time to pet?**

A:

* Aww! Great idea.
* I think we shouldn’t sign up Mark for making more art…

**Q: Why isn't there an option for all friends to be together instead of voting for a pair :(**

A: It would be too powerful

## Puzzles

**Q: Were there any differences backstage in how you wrote and edited the puzzles this year?**

A: Over the last few years, we’ve successfully anchored our puzzle writing and testing around a few major writing/testing weekends. This year we had:

* After the theme is decided, ~1 month to write metapuzzles
* Writing retreat: brainstorm remaining metas and jumpstart writing puzzles for the tested metas
* Small Big Test Solve: tested all metas
* Medium Big Test Solve: goal was to test 15/40 puzzles, but this ended up being a puzzle writing weekend
* Big Big Test Solve: full-hunt testsolve by people outside of the GPH26 Discord server

**Q: Was including two DJ answers that started with PINK an intentional red herring? Er, pink herring?**

A: Many people noticed the answer PINK FLOYD used in Personality Conflict was a red herring for the trans flag colors in Figuration. We discussed trying to replace it, but we didn’t like the alternative answers we found, and decided that some additional difficulty in metamatching was the preferable option.

**Q: Why Great Expectations??**

A: This puzzle was written around its answer (SATIS House). I thought a large data file (relative to most puzzles) would be interesting. There’s not a lot more to say.

**Q: I'm really curious how you came up with the novels/movies for Personal Flying Monkeys such that THESOURCE and WHITEGLUE both came out of it so perfectly.**

A: The two target phrases were decided first, then it was brute-force looking at the possible options for each pair of works, to see what question/index combinations can give the needed letter pairs.

**Q: How many stories about spoiling peoples' Wordles did y'all receive?**

*Note: The post-solve dialogue for Wordtris gave out that day’s Wordle answer.*

A: Exactly one, from you.

## Web

**Q: How was the scoreboard split up?**

A: During the hunt, the scoreboard was organized into groups of at least 10 teams, sorted by number of puzzles solved. After the hunt, teams were grouped by which day they solved the final metameta.

**Q: I'd love to hear how the interactive tool for Grid Adventure worked! And if y'all were interested in posting an open source version others could use that would be amazing! Relatedly, when will we get an open source version of your brand new hunt website framework (which is mentioned in 2024 wrap-up)?**

A: The interactive puzzles since 2023 have been built on top of the same flexible base. We’ve been talking about open-sourcing the new, Node-based version of the GPH codebase for a while now, but haven’t gotten around to it yet. Thanks for your interest and your reminder.

**Q: I was looking through some of the solutions and there's some really fancy features that didn't exist before — are there new tools now or are y’all just really locked in on super cool solution pages?**

A: Our stellar web team put in a lot of work with Claude Code to bring the solutions alive.

**Q: How did you choose this font with the funky lowercase "a" character?**

A: My original vision of the graphic identity was a hippie retro psychedelic 60s look. Hence the rainbow gradients, the pink text outlines, the wavy grid background, and a font with the same vibes as Cooper Black.

**Q: Of the hunts done so far, which has been your favorite (in terms of idea, puzzle design, implementation, etc. whatever really lol)?**

A: I can’t speak for everyone on the team, but personally I really liked [Stargazing](https://2024.galacticpuzzlehunt.com) for its innovative micropuzzle design.
